speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the current range of waiting time for enrolment in childcare centres; (b) whether there is a shortage of childcare teachers currently and, if so, what is the Ministry doing to increase the number of childcare teachers; and (c) whether a comprehensive study has been done on the needs of childcare centres and how their capacity can be maximised.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: In particular, parents may have to wait longer if they prefer a specific centre due to its location, operator or other reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: A fair proportion of the children in the queues for the more popular centres are already enrolled in some other centres.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To further reduce waiting times, we will continue to inject more childcare capacity in housing estates with high demand.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: This includes the four recently announced large centres in Punggol, Sengkang and Bukit Panjang.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Future HDB Build-To-Order (BTO) housing developments have also been planned with larger childcare centres to meet the needs of our young families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Over the past few years, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) has been working closely with operators and training agencies on various initiatives to attract, retain and also develop our educators.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Last October, ECDA launched a comprehensive Early Childhood Manpower Plan to provide more professional development opportunities for early childhood educators, a more supportive working environment and greater respect and recognition for educators.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: To understand and address ground challenges, ECDA conducts very regular consultations with the sector, including townhall sessions, surveys and centre visits.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: For example, the Early Childhood Manpower Plan was developed in consultation with key sector partners, such as unions, industry associations and operators.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: ECDA will continue to work closely and collaboratively with the sector.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The reason I raise this question is because almost every other week, I receive feedback from residents requesting for help.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My first question is: are there any plans to review the salary of teachers?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It seems that from the operators, they told me there is a shortage of teachers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And when I talk to the teachers, they said there is a disparity in the salary between childcare teachers and the school teachers, although they are both degree holders.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Second, would there be any more new mega childcare centres in Yishun, because the one that we have, I understand, is fully subscribed?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Third, will the Ministry work with HDB to have bigger childcare centres for new BTOs, because in every new BTO, the childcare capacity is only about 100, which is insufficient?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The last question is, will the Ministry work with HDB to have the childcare centre in a new BTO to be in operation when they hand over the keys, because there is always a delay?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: After a few months, then the childcare centre is in operation.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Perhaps, let me just give a perspective about waiting time for children to be enrolled in childcare centres.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do acknowledge that in certain estates, there is high demand and a bit of mismatch, but perhaps just let me give context as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, in hotspot areas, such as Punggol and Sengkang, it ranges from a few weeks to a few months.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are a range of factors that affect waiting time.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: About 40% of them are currently enrolled in a childcare centre but whose parents indicated preference for another centre.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But for first-timers themselves as well, some may also be queuing ahead of time and not necessarily having an immediate childcare need.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When we say that there is a waiting list, there are a range of reasons as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But specifically, we do know that in high-demand areas, there are certain concerns.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: One of the areas that the Member had raised is with regard to salary.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Salary is one factor in terms of attracting people into the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA regularly undertakes manpower surveys to help operators better understand the wage levels and human resource practices across the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The findings are shared, so that we can encourage operators to keep up with human resource practices and to make sure that they remain competitive.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We understand that salaries have shifted upwards, led by the Anchor Operators (AOPs).

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is something that we are working on with the AOPs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Salaries for entry-level diploma trained teachers are also comparable to other sectors and competitive.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do recognise that salaries do play an important part and we should endeavour to see how best to raise that where possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Beyond salaries, there are also a range of initiatives to recognise and develop the teachers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, the Skills Framework for Early Childhood Care and Education spells out the career pathways, specific skills and competencies required for various job roles and, therefore, encouraging competency-based career development for educators.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Also, the Professional Development Programme and the ECDA Fellows Scheme select competent preschool teachers and exemplary leaders respectively to contribute to the centres or sector and recognise their work through awards and allowances.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are a range of measures that we are putting in place through the Manpower Plan to try to level up and make sure that the sector is attractive, so that we can draw more people into the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This was announced last year at the Committee of Supply 2015.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is to provide accessible, affordable and quality childcare services.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Each centre can take 300 to 500 children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Four large childcare centres in Punggol, Yishun, Sengkang and Woodlands have started operations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The remaining centre in Jurong West will commence operations in the first quarter of 2017.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We continue to work very closely with stakeholders, as I mentioned earlier, to review the demand and provide the spaces where possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Going forward, what we are doing is to work very closely with HDB.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will be revisiting the planning norms to make sure that HDB estates, as they emerge, especially with a younger profile, the demand for childcare places can be met by increasing the number of places.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The other question, which is a pertinent one, because I experienced it myself as well, is that when the HDB flats are ready, can the childcare centres be ready at the same time?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is also something that we are working closely with HDB on, to try to minimise that gap between when the flats and centres are ready.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But as Members also realise, for flats, when they are ready, actually the people are streaming in over a fairly long period of time, perhaps up to six to nine months.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do recognise that we should try to get it ready as far as possible, so that when the families come in, the childcare centres or the kindergartens can be operational as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would just like to clarify, earlier the Minister mentioned that his Ministry is increasing the capacity of training in the polytechnics for early childhood educators.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I wonder if the Ministry has a dedicated policy to also expand the capacity in privately-run operations, whether it is the SEED Institute, KLC International Institute and the other institutes that train early childhood educators.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will we be also expanding their capacity, so that the pipeline of teachers coming into the industry will be ensured?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do have very direct levers with our institutions of education.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to the polytechnics, we are increasing the capacity.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With the private institutions, we are discussing with them on the various measures and we will continue to collaborate with them where possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: If we are able to increase the capacity, we will be more than happy to see that happen.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Because the one that the Minister mentioned, yes, it is in operation and it is over-subscribed, long queue.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When we are ready, we will be more than happy to let Members know in advance of time.
